verses.zh: 约书亚将以色列的众支派聚集在示剑，召了以色列的长老、族长、审判官，并官长来，他们就站在　神面前。
verses.en: Joshua assembled all the Israelite tribes at Shechem. He summoned Israel’s elders, rulers, judges, and leaders, and they appeared before God.

verses.zh: 约书亚对众民说：「耶和华―以色列的　神如此说：『古时你们的列祖，就是亚伯拉罕和拿鹤的父亲他拉，住在大河那边事奉别神，
verses.en: Joshua told all the people, “This is what the Lord God of Israel has said: ‘In the distant past your ancestors lived beyond the Euphrates River,[NOTE:1] including Terah the father of Abraham and Nahor. They worshiped[NOTE:2] other gods,
notes: Heb “the river,” referring to the Euphrates. This has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “served.”

verses.zh: 我将你们的祖宗亚伯拉罕从大河那边带来，领他走遍迦南全地，又使他的子孙众多，把以撒赐给他；
verses.en: but I took your father Abraham from beyond the Euphrates[NOTE:1] and brought him into[NOTE:2] the entire land of Canaan. I made his descendants numerous; I gave him Isaac,
notes: Heb “the river,” referring to the Euphrates. This has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “through.”

verses.zh: 又把雅各和以扫赐给以撒，将西珥山赐给以扫为业；后来雅各和他的子孙下到埃及去了。
verses.en: and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. To Esau I assigned Mount Seir,[NOTE:1] while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
notes: Heb “I gave to Esau Mount Seir to possess it.”

verses.zh: 我差遣摩西、亚伦，并照我在埃及中所行的降灾与埃及，然后把你们领出来。
verses.en: I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt down when I intervened in their land.[NOTE:1] Then I brought you out.
notes: Heb “by that which I did in its midst.”

verses.zh: 我领你们列祖出埃及，他们就到了红海；埃及人带领车辆马兵追赶你们列祖到红海。
verses.en: When I brought your fathers out of Egypt, you arrived at the sea. The Egyptians chased your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.

verses.zh: 你们列祖哀求耶和华，他就使你们和埃及人中间黑暗了，又使海水淹没埃及人。我在埃及所行的事，你们亲眼见过。你们在旷野也住了许多年日。
verses.en: Your fathers[NOTE:1] cried out for help to the Lord; he made the area between you and the Egyptians dark,[NOTE:2] and then he drowned them in the sea.[NOTE:3] You witnessed with your very own eyes[NOTE:4] what I did in Egypt. You lived in the wilderness for a long time.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (the fathers) has been specified in the translation for clarity (see the previous verse).
Or “put darkness between you and the Egyptians.”
Heb “and he brought over them the sea and covered them.”
Heb “your eyes saw.”
Heb “many days.”

verses.zh: 我领你们到约旦河东亚摩利人所住之地。他们与你们争战，我将他们交在你们手中，你们便得了他们的地为业；我也在你们面前将他们灭绝。
verses.en: Then I brought you to the land of the Amorites who lived east of the Jordan. They fought with you, but I handed them over to you; you conquered[NOTE:1] their land, and I destroyed them from before you.
notes: Or “took possession of.”

verses.zh: 那时，摩押王西拨的儿子巴勒起来攻击以色列人，打发人召了比珥的儿子巴兰来咒诅你们。
verses.en: Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, launched an attack[NOTE:1] against Israel. He summoned[NOTE:2] Balaam son of Beor to call down judgment on[NOTE:3] you.
notes: Heb “arose and fought.”
Heb “sent and called.”
Or “to curse.”

verses.zh: 我不肯听巴兰的话，所以他倒为你们连连祝福。这样，我便救你们脱离巴勒的手。
verses.en: I refused to respond to Balaam; he kept[NOTE:1] prophesying good things about[NOTE:2] you, and I rescued you from his power.[NOTE:3]
notes: The infinitive absolute follows the finite verb in the Hebrew text and indicates continuation or repetition of the action. Balaam pronounced several oracles of blessing over Israel (see Num 23-24).
Heb “blessing.” Balaam’s “blessings” were actually prophecies of how God would prosper Israel.
Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 你们过了约旦河，到了耶利哥；耶利哥人、亚摩利人、比利洗人、迦南人、赫人、革迦撒人、希未人、耶布斯人都与你们争战；我把他们交在你们手里。
verses.en: You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho.[NOTE:1] The leaders[NOTE:2] of Jericho, as well as the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites, fought against you, but I handed them over to you.
notes: For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
Or perhaps, “citizens.”

verses.zh: 我打发黄蜂飞在你们前面，将亚摩利人的二王从你们面前撵出，并不是用你的刀，也不是用你的弓。
verses.en: I sent terror[NOTE:1] ahead of you to drive out before you the two[NOTE:2] Amorite kings. I gave you the victory; it was not by your swords or bows.[NOTE:3]
notes: Traditionally, “the hornet” (so KJV, NKJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV) but the precise meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain (cf. NEB “panic”).
The LXX has “twelve,” apparently understanding this as a reference to Amorite kings west of the Jordan (see Josh 5:1, rather than the trans-Jordanian Amorite kings Sihon and Og (see Josh 2:10; 9:10).
Heb “and it drove them out from before you, the two kings of the Amorites, not by your sword and not by your bow.” The words “I gave you the victory” are supplied for clarification.

verses.zh: 我赐给你们地土，非你们所修治的；我赐给你们城邑，非你们所建造的。你们就住在其中，又得吃非你们所栽种的葡萄园、橄榄园的果子。』
verses.en: I gave you a land in[NOTE:1] which you had not worked hard; you took up residence in cities you did not build, and you are eating the produce of[NOTE:2] vineyards and olive groves you did not plant.’
notes: Or perhaps, “for.”
The words “the produce of” are supplied for clarification.

verses.zh: 「现在你们要敬畏耶和华，诚心<WAHb>实意地<WAHb>事奉他，将你们列祖在大河那边和在埃及所事奉的神除掉，去事奉耶和华。
verses.en: “Now[NOTE:1] obey[NOTE:2] the Lord and worship[NOTE:3] him with integrity and loyalty. Put aside the gods your ancestors[NOTE:4] worshiped[NOTE:5] beyond the Euphrates[NOTE:6] and in Egypt, and worship[NOTE:7] the Lord.
notes: Joshua quotes the Lord’s words in vv. 2b-13 (note that the Lord speaks in the first person in these verses); in vv. 14-15 Joshua himself exhorts the people (note the third person references to the Lord).
Heb “fear.”
Or “and serve.”
Heb “your fathers.”
Or “served.”
Heb “the river,” referring to the Euphrates. This has been specified in the translation for clarity; see v. 3.
Or “and serve.”

verses.zh: 若是你们以事奉耶和华为不好，今日就可以选择所要事奉的：是你们列祖在大河那边所事奉的神呢？是你们所住这地的亚摩利人的神呢？至于我和我家，我们必定事奉耶和华。」
verses.en: If you have no desire[NOTE:1] to worship[NOTE:2] the Lord, then choose today whom you will worship,[NOTE:3] whether it be the gods whom your ancestors[NOTE:4] worshiped[NOTE:5] beyond the Euphrates[NOTE:6] or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living. But I and my family[NOTE:7] will worship[NOTE:8] the Lord.”
notes: Heb “if it is bad in your eyes.”
Or “to serve.”
Or “will serve.”
Heb “your fathers.”
Or “served.”
Heb “the river,” referring to the Euphrates. This has been specified in the translation for clarity; see v. 3.
Heb “house.”
Or “will serve.”

verses.zh: 百姓回答说：「我们断不敢离弃耶和华去事奉别神；
verses.en: The people responded, “Far be it from us to abandon the Lord so we can[NOTE:1] worship[NOTE:2] other gods!
notes: Heb “to.”
Or “can serve.”

verses.zh: 因耶和华―我们的　神曾将我们和我们列祖从埃及地的为奴之家领出来，在我们眼前行了那些大神迹，在我们所行的道上，所经过的诸国，都保护了我们。
verses.en: For the Lord our God took us and our fathers out of slavery[NOTE:1] in the land of Egypt[NOTE:2] and performed these awesome miracles[NOTE:3] before our very eyes. He continually protected us as we traveled and when we passed through nations.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “of the house of slavery.”
Heb “for the Lord our God, he is the one who brought up us and our fathers from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.”
Or “great signs.”
Heb “and he guarded us in all the way in which we walked and among all the peoples through whose midst we passed.”

verses.zh: 耶和华又把住此地的亚摩利人都从我们面前赶出去。所以，我们必事奉耶和华，因为他是我们的　神。」
verses.en: The Lord drove out from before us all the nations, including the Amorites who lived in the land. So we too will worship[NOTE:1] the Lord, for he is our God!”
notes: Or “will serve.”

verses.zh: 约书亚对百姓说：「你们不能事奉耶和华；因为他是圣洁的　神，是忌邪的　神，必不赦免你们的过犯罪恶。
verses.en: Joshua warned[NOTE:1] the people, “You will not keep worshiping[NOTE:2] the Lord, for[NOTE:3] he is a holy God.[NOTE:4] He is a jealous God who will not forgive[NOTE:5] your rebellion or your sins.
notes: Heb “said to.”
Heb “you are not able to serve.”
For an excellent discussion of Joshua’s logical argument here, see T. C. Butler, Joshua (WBC), 274-75.

In the Hebrew text both the divine name (אֱלֹהִים, ʾelohim) and the adjective (קְדֹשִׁים, qedoshim, “holy”) are plural. Normally the divine name, when referring to the one true God, takes singular modifiers, but this is a rare exception where the adjective agrees grammatically with the honorific plural noun. See GKC §124.i and IBHS 122.

This assertion obviously needs qualification, for the OT elsewhere affirms that God does forgive. Joshua is referring to the persistent national rebellion against the Mosaic covenant that eventually causes God to decree unconditionally the nation’s exile.tn Heb “lift up” or “take away.”

verses.zh: 你们若离弃耶和华去事奉外邦神，耶和华在降福之后，必转而降祸与你们，把你们灭绝。」
verses.en: If[NOTE:1] you abandon the Lord and worship[NOTE:2] foreign gods, he will turn against you;[NOTE:3] he will bring disaster on you and destroy you,[NOTE:4] though he once treated you well.”[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “when.”
Or “and serve.”
The words “against you” are added for clarification.
Heb “bring you to an end.”
Heb “after he did good for you.”

verses.zh: 百姓回答约书亚说：「不然，我们定要事奉耶和华。」
verses.en: The people said to Joshua, “No! We really will[NOTE:1] worship[NOTE:2] the Lord.”
notes: The translation assumes that כִּי (ki) is emphatic. Another option is to take it as explanatory, “No, for we will….”
Or “will serve.”

verses.zh: 约书亚对百姓说：「你们选定耶和华，要事奉他，你们自己作见证吧！」他们说：「我们愿意作见证。」
verses.en: Joshua said to the people, “Do you agree to be witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen to worship the Lord?”[NOTE:1] They replied, “We are witnesses!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen for yourselves the Lord to serve him.”
Like witnesses in a court of law, Israel’s solemn vow to worship the Lord will testify against them in the divine court if the nation ever violates its commitment.

verses.zh: 约书亚说：「你们现在要除掉你们中间的外邦神，专心归向耶和华―以色列的　神。」
verses.en: Joshua said,[NOTE:1] “Now put aside the foreign gods that are among you and submit to[NOTE:2] the Lord God of Israel.”
notes: The words “Joshua said” are supplied for clarification.
Heb “bend your heart toward.” The term לֵבָב (levav, “heart”) probably here refers to the people’s volition or will.

verses.zh: 百姓回答约书亚说：「我们必事奉耶和华―我们的　神，听从他的话。」
verses.en: The people said to Joshua, “We will worship[NOTE:1] the Lord our God and obey him.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “will serve.”
Heb “and listen to his voice.”

verses.zh: 当日，约书亚就与百姓立约，在示剑为他们立定律例典章。
verses.en: That day Joshua drew up an agreement[NOTE:1] for the people, and he established rules and regulations[NOTE:2] for them in Shechem.
notes: Heb “cut a covenant.”
Heb “a statute and a judgment.”

verses.zh: 约书亚将这些话都写在　神的律法书上，又将一块大石头立在橡树下耶和华的圣所旁边。
verses.en: Joshua wrote these words in the Law Scroll of God. He then took a large stone and set it up there under the oak tree near the Lord’s sanctuary.

verses.zh: 约书亚对百姓说：「看哪，这石头可以向我们作见证；因为是听见了耶和华所吩咐我们的一切话，倘或你们背弃你们的　神，这石头就可以向你们作见证（倘或...见证：或译所以要向你们作见证，免得你们背弃耶和华―你们的　神）。」
verses.en: Joshua said to all the people, “Look, this stone will be a witness against us, for it has heard everything the Lord said to us.[NOTE:1] It will be a witness against you if[NOTE:2] you deny your God.”
notes: Heb “all the words of the Lord which he spoke with us.”
Or “lest,” “so that you might not.”

verses.zh: 于是约书亚打发百姓各归自己的地业去了。
verses.en: When Joshua dismissed the people, they went to their allotted portions of land.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And Joshua sent the people away, each to his inheritance.”

verses.zh: 这些事以后，耶和华的仆人嫩的儿子约书亚，正一百一十岁，就死了。
verses.en: After all this[NOTE:1] Joshua son of Nun, the Lord’s servant, died at the age of 110.
notes: Heb “after these things.”

verses.zh: 以色列人将他葬在他地业的境内，就是在以法莲山地的亭拿・西拉，在迦实山的北边。
verses.en: They buried him in his allotted territory[NOTE:1] in Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
notes: Heb “in the territory of his inheritance.”

verses.zh: 约书亚在世和约书亚死后，那些知道耶和华为以色列人所行诸事的长老还在的时候，以色列人事奉耶和华。
verses.en: Israel worshiped[NOTE:1] the Lord throughout Joshua’s lifetime and as long as the elderly men who outlived him remained alive.[NOTE:2] These men had experienced firsthand everything the Lord had done for Israel.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “served.”
Heb “all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived him.”
Heb “who knew all the work of the Lord which he had done for Israel.”

verses.zh: 以色列人从埃及所带来约瑟的骸骨，葬埋在示剑，就是在雅各从前用一百块银子向示剑的父亲、哈抹的子孙所买的那块地里；这就作了约瑟子孙的产业。
verses.en: The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem in the part of the field that Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for 100 pieces of money.[NOTE:1] So it became the inheritance of the tribe of Joseph.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “one hundred qesitahs.” The Hebrew word קְשִׂיטָה (qesitah) is generally understood to refer to a unit of money, but the value and/or weight is unknown. The word occurs only here and in Gen 33:19 and Job 42:11.

Heb “and they became for the sons of Joseph an inheritance.” One might think “bones” is the subject of the verb “they became,” but the verb is masculine, while “bones” is feminine. The translation follows the emendation suggested in the BHS note, which appeals to the Syriac and Vulgate for support. The emended reading understands “the part (of the field)” as the subject of the verb “became.” The emended verb is feminine singular; this agrees with “the part” (of the field), which is feminine in Hebrew.

verses.zh: 亚伦的儿子以利亚撒也死了，就把他葬在他儿子非尼哈所得以法莲山地的小山上。
verses.en: Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him in Gibeah in the hill country of Ephraim, where his son Phinehas had been assigned land.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in Gibeah of Phinehas, his son, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.”
